questions.question: You are driving in the left lane with two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right. What should you do if a driver behind you wants to go faster?

options.text: Stay in your lane to keep traffic flowing.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let vehicles pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to pass or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than other traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Touch one rear wheel to the curb.
Use your parking brake and put the vehicle in "park."
Point your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and put the vehicle in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and put the vehicle in "park" when parking on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your wheels away from the center of the road. If there is a curb, point your wheels toward it (going downhill) or gently toward it (going uphill).

questions.question: You are behind a motorcycle and want to pass. What must you do?

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and doesn't need the full lane.
Honk to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Move entirely into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move entirely into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give a motorcycle a full lane when passing. Never share the same lane while passing. Returning to your lane too soon can force the rider to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your vehicle and the one in front?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, or vehicles with trailers may not see you directly behind them. Increase your following distance with these vehicles. Large vehicles also block your view of the road, so stay back to see around them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are traveling in the wrong direction.
Treat the intersection like a stop sign.
You cannot go until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Road work or maintenance is happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road work or maintenance is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs mark construction and maintenance work areas. They help drivers and pedestrians stay safe. Fines for traffic violations may double in these areas.

questions.question: Your car's rear end starts skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This straightens out your vehicle.

questions.question: A vehicle cuts in front of you, creating danger. What is your first action?

options.text: Honk and brake firmly.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle cuts in front of you, release the gas pedal. This creates space without hard braking or swerving into another lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crosswalk. Watch for pedestrians crossing the road.

questions.question: You miss your exit on the freeway. What should you not do?

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your correct exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on the road or shoulder if you miss your exit. Continue to the next exit or crossroad. Other drivers do not expect vehicles to back up, which causes accidents.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slower.

questions.question: In rainy weather, you should be most careful when turning or stopping:

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when turning and stopping during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars mixes with the rain, making the road slippery.

questions.question: If you are continually being passed on the right and left while driving in the center lane of an expressway, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the lane on your right.
Move to the lane on your left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the lane on your right.
questions.explanation: On a road with four or more lanes, use the right lanes except when passing or turning left. On an interstate, use the right lane if you are driving slower than the traffic around you.

questions.question: If you are being passed in a no passing zone, you should:

options.text: Pull off the road.
Maintain your speed and position.
Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down to help the passing vehicle return to the drive lane safely. This helps everyone avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. Yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a "Walk" signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other vehicles that have a green light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction/maintenance area.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction/maintenance area.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange signs are used for construction and maintenance areas.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Prepare to stop, if needed.
Maintain a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop, if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill. Slow down so you can stop if a vehicle is stalled ahead. Always adjust your speed before going over a hill or around a curve.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the road instead of into traffic.

questions.question: If you find yourself in a skid:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake abruptly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, do not use the brakes. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
Turn on your high beam headlights to better see the vehicles ahead of you.
Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, where should you drive?

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, drive in the lane closest to the centerline. Start your turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: Motorcycles do not follow the same traffic rules as other vehicles.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
Motorcycles brake more slowly than regular vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop quickly. Following too closely puts your life and the motorcyclist's life at risk. You need enough time and space to avoid a crash if the motorcyclist makes a sudden stop.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. When can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: When you increase your speed before the turn.
When traffic on that street moves to the right.
When traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street if traffic moves to the left and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road as close as possible and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road as close as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. Move again after the emergency vehicle has passed.

questions.question: Which statement is true about road work zones?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as fines for normal traffic violations.
You must slow down in work zones.
Slow down only if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in work zones.
questions.explanation: Always reduce your speed in work zones and be ready to slow down or stop for equipment. Driving carefully through work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and workers safe.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has rained hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery during the first half hour of rain. Water mixes with oil and chemicals on the road that have not yet washed away. Use extra caution when roads are wet.

questions.question: If you don't see a gap in freeway traffic when entering, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.
Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp if you don't see a space in traffic. Do not wait at the end of the ramp because you won't have enough room to speed up before entering the freeway.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, your body will be thrown backward. Brace yourself by pressing against your seat and putting your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: When leaving an alley or driveway to cross a sidewalk, what should drivers do?

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to yield the right-of-way to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop before driving onto a sidewalk when leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot. Pedestrians and traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then enter when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow to a safe speed and cross the intersection with caution.
